title: The Scientist Who Won Twice
paragraphs: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw in eighteen sixty seven, at a time when women could not study at the university there. She moved to Paris to continue her education, and in eighteen ninety four she met Pierre Curie, a physicist whose laboratory she began to use. They married the following year and began working side by side. Her determination to learn shaped everything that followed.

The couple became interested in the spontaneous radiation that Henri Becquerel had discovered. Working with a heavy ore called pitchblende, they noticed that it was more radioactive than uranium alone could explain. They concluded that it must contain other radioactive substances, and they eventually extracted two new elements: polonium, named after her native Poland, and radium. Their work was slow and physically demanding.

In nineteen oh three, Marie and Pierre shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Becquerel. After Pierre's death in nineteen oh six, she took over his professorship, and in nineteen eleven she received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry on her own. To this day, she remains the only person to have won Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields. Her life shows how curiosity and persistence can change science.
